name: distrust
quote: They've screwed up my order too often.
description: A solid sense that someone or something has a low likelihood of conforming to a particular prediction.
perceptions: This person, group, idea, or tool is supposed behave in a certain way.
My sense is that the odds of this outcome are so low that I'm not willing to base my actions on it.
results: The predicted outcome may occur or it might not. Either way, future prediction patterns may change.
examples: assuming your kid will waste too much time with video games
not trusting the government agency to finish the permit on time
I don't think that low tire is going to make it to the service station.

comparisons.description: Pessimism focuses more on the general outcome, for example, that you're probably going to lose the game. Distrust is about specific things, for instance, that you have bad luck or that your opponent is probably going to cheat.

variations.name: suspicion
variations.description: An uncertain sense that someone or something has a chance of surprising you in some way, often negative.
perceptions: This person, group, idea, or tool is socially expected to behave in a certain way.
There's something weird about what's actually happening.
results: A suspicion may lead to anxiety about a negative outcome, or less often it may hint about something positive.

guidance.description: Suspicion can indicate a problem of trust in a relationship.
This article has advice for recognizing suspicious individuals in the workplace.

examples: It's weird that stranger seems to be following us.

comparisons.description: 'Distrust' is when you're certain enough to take action. 'Suspicion' is a distrust that is still doubtful.

commentaries.quote: Trust and distrust in new area is based on generalizing characteristics from something similar we do have experience with. Yes, this is basically stereotyping, and it's the way the brain handles the unknown. What matters is the manner of how we approach someone that is not initially trusted.

Low trust is the greatest cost in life and in organizations, including families. Low trust creates hidden agendas, politics, interpersonal conflict, interdepartmental rivalries, win-lose thinking, defensive and protective communication.
